name: gzip
description: Compresses a single file, replacing it with file.gz. Decompress with gunzip or gzip -d.

flags.description: Keep the original file (default replaces it!).
Write to stdout, leaving the original intact (for pipes).

examples.explanation: Compresses to big.log.gz and REMOVES the original. Use -k to keep it.
Both files exist afterwards (shown via ls).
Maximum compression — slower but smallest result.
Compresses via pipe without touching the source file.

about: gzip compresses single files, not directories (use tar for that). It is fast and universally supported; zstd and xz offer better ratios or speed but with varying availability. Decompression: gunzip file.gz or zcat file.gz to read without extracting.
mistakes: Losing originals by forgetting -k — plain gzip replaces files.
Trying to gzip a directory — tar first.
